current.text: He is a rookie and is projected to start at forward for Memphis, with Ty Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jerami Grant and Zach Edey.
He is projected for about 30 to 32 minutes, one of only two Grizzlies above 30. One expert says 33 minutes would make him an easy top 50 player.
Ja Morant was traded to Portland. Ty Jerome starts at point guard, and Memphis is giving him a big role.
With Morant gone, he should take the first or second playmaking role in Memphis, and his assist rate should go up.
He looked very good in his first preseason game. At Summer League he averaged 17 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists, a steal and a three on 51% FG, 82% FT and 40% from three.
Experts expect him to be the best fantasy rookie this season, with immediate impact because of how the Memphis roster is built.

He is expected to start slowly, with early efficiency struggles like Cooper Flagg had, and to do more as the season goes on. The newest view has him outside the top 70 at first and top 35 in February and March. Other experts expect a top 25 to 30 level by the fantasy playoffs.
In mock drafts he goes almost always around the start of round 5. He went 54th in one mock and for 15 USD in an auction mock.
His fair draft range is the 50s to 60s. A pick inside the top 50, or his Yahoo rank of 51, is a bit early but not terrible.
His stock is rising after a strong preseason. One expert pushed him up, another wanted him as a target at pick 54, and one expert's auction max was 15 USD.
Coach Tuomas Iisalo plays at a very high pace, uses short, hard stints and keeps minutes down. Memphis is expected to run an 11 or 12 man rotation.
Memphis has a maxed 4-4-4 schedule in our playoff weeks (season end March 28) and only 13 back-to-backs, possibly the fewest in the league.
Memphis is expected to be fairly bad, around low to mid 30s wins, but not to tank.
Memphis has an overcrowded roster and three 2027 first-round picks, which gives it room to make trades, including moving Jerami Grant.

durable.text: He does nearly everything: points, rebounds, assists, steals, solid free throws, good FG% and threes. Experts call him an excellent passer and a scalable player.
He has limits as a rim protector and is likely to lack blocks.
He plays more like a small forward than a center, with point forward potential.
He had a 30 usage rate at Duke with high assist numbers.
He is not expected to be a 30 usage player in the NBA.
Projections make threes and turnovers his two weakest categories for a forward. Rebounds are his best category. The sites split on threes: Yahoo projects 1.3 per game, ESPN 0.3.

note: Boozer is the top rookie, but his value comes late. The experts see him outside the top 70 early and at a top 25 to 35 level by the playoffs, and Memphis has a maxed 4-4-4 playoff schedule. Yahoo's average cost is 10.2 USD, ESPN's is 7.3 USD, and an auction mock went 15 USD, so 10 to 15 USD fits his 50s to 60s fair range. Going higher means paying for a preseason buzz that is still rising. He fits punt TO builds and may fit punt 3PM builds. Early on, check his minutes in Iisalo's short-stint rotation, and see whether his threes look like Yahoo's 1.3 per game or ESPN's 0.3.
